thread:
Alex Chen: Quick follow-up from the PM: eviction surge yesterday. We fixed the immediate regression but need a clear set of runbook updates + owners for remediation.
Maya Patel: I'll take the runbook rewrite. Plan to add a short triage checklist and exact commands to reduce ambiguity for oncall.
Ben Ortiz: Please include the KV shard checks and the autoscaler debug steps. Off the top of my head:
```
kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide --selector=app=inference
kubectl -n inference exec -it svc-inference-0 -- sh -c 'cat /proc/pressure/memory || dmesg | tail -n 200'
curl -sS http://localhost:9090/metrics | grep kv_cache_hit_ratio
```
Also capture node allocatable vs usage and eviction_score from kubelet logs.
Sienna Ko: I'll own the remediation epic. Short timeline proposal: 2-day spike for cache TTL + batch cap experiments, then a 10-day sprint focused on autoscaler tuning and graceful degrade. Spike results due EOD Thu.
Priya Singh: I'll pair with Sienna on the autoscaler canary config — need to validate with Dedicated infra before we change global thresholds.
Alex Chen: Good. In the runbook we should add clear escalation thresholds. Suggest:
- page @sre-oncall when >3 pods from the same node pool evicted within 10m
- page @infra-lead if model fallback triggers more than twice in 1h
- open INF ticket and assign remediation owner if user-facing error rate >0.5% for 15m
Maya Patel: I'll add those thresholds verbatim. Also adding a canned Slack template for the oncall to post in #incidents with key diagnostics attached.
Ben Ortiz: Add automated checks: PromQL snippets to paste in runbook so oncall can copy-paste into Prometheus UI:
```
sum(rate(kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason{reason=\"OOMKilled\"}[5m])) by (node)
(kube_pod_container_resource_requests_cpu_cores + kube_pod_container_resource_requests_memory_bytes) / node_namespace_pod:kube_pod_info:count
```
Sienna Ko: For remediation tasks: Sienna -> spike + experiments; Priya -> canary autoscaler; Ben -> runbook automation & alerts; Maya -> runbook doc + PR. I'll create the epic INF-4990 and break into subtasks.
Ops Bot: Created INF-4990 \"Eviction surge: runbook + remediation\" and linked to postmortem. Subtasks created for spike, canary, runbook PR, and alerting.
Priya Singh: One more: add a short rollback recipe for autoscaler and batching changes: how to revert and how to validate a rollback.
Maya Patel: Noted. I'll add rollback steps, a minimal post-change validation checklist (p99 latency, kv hit ratio, and no further evictions in 30m).
Alex Chen: Also add a short regression eval that watches model quality when fallback model is used — we saw a small drop yesterday. Define success criteria and the notification path if quality drops >1%.
Ben Ortiz: I'll author the alert rule drafts and attach example PATTERN match queries to the runbook. Also adding a new synthetic that runs a small prompt set against the fallback route.
Sienna Ko: Spike update: we'll try TTLs 15s/30s/60s and batch caps 48/56/64 during load tests. Load test scheduled Fri 09:00 PT. If we see steady eviction reduction with <1% latency increase, we'll pick the best candidate for the sprint.
Maya Patel: Runbook PR target: open by Fri EOD, include triage steps, commands, PromQLs, escalation thresholds, canned Slack text, and rollback recipe.
Alex Chen: OK. Action summary for tracker: 1) Runbook PR (Maya) by Fri EOD, 2) Spike + load test (Sienna) by Fri 09:00 PT, 3) Canary autoscaler change (Priya) target next Wed, 4) Alert rules and synthetic (Ben) by next Wed. Update INF-4990 with due dates.
Priya Singh: I'll sync with Dedicated infra today and post any blockers in the ticket.
Ben Ortiz: After PR lands I'll add a small automation script that outputs the minimal diagnostics bundle for the oncall to paste in the incident thread.
Alex Chen: Thanks all. Let's reconvene Fri 11:30 PT after the load test to decide sprint scope. Adding calendar invite. :white_check_mark:
